transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (NexaHealth Head of Data), Tom Alvarez (NexaHealth SRE), Priya Singh (NexaHealth PM)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on onboarding and env readiness; small pilot results reviewed; agreed actions on security docs and VPC peering.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays week—I'll keep this short. Quick roll call — Samir here from Redwood, Elena's with me,
[00:06] Elena: hi all, Elena, SE, glad to be here
[00:09] Lena: Lena Park on my side, morning
[00:11] Tom: Tom Alvarez, SRE
[00:13] Priya: Priya here, PM
[00:18] Samir: Cool, agenda: 1) access and peering status, 2) env readiness and GPU access + images, 3) quick review of small benchmark we ran, 4) tuning recommendations, 5) next steps.

[00:33] Tom: Quick note, we tried the SSH into the bastion this morning but hit a firewall rule we missed, so peering hasn't been completed yet, we should be able to open the port later today
[00:41] Elena: ok that maps to what we saw — the test worker couldn't reach the redis KV endpoint because of that, so some of the end-to-end tests failed.
[00:47] Lena: And just to be clear, we ran the sample 1k token inference on the hosted endpoint and it was fine, but when we tried the 5k burst tests against the dedicated pool we saw p99 latency spikes.
[00:58] Samir: Right, that's consistent. The 1k tests are mostly single-token loops so they look great. The p99 spikes at 5k are the interesting part. Elena, quick explanation?
[01:07] Elena: yeah, so two things likely: one, the batch sizing we used was fairly large which increases tail latency for certain requests; two, we didn't have prefix/KV cache enabled in the test harness so we're missing the cache hit benefits for repeated context. Also I noticed the quantized model we loaded was 4-bit but with a slower kernel path on the particular GPU type you have. Might be the driver/kernel selection. There were a couple of warnings in the runtime about kernel fallback, which increases latency.
[01:33] Tom: Hmm driver issues — what GPU are we actually on in the dedicated pool?
[01:37] Samir: According to the config you requested it's A100s, but the staging dedicated node we spun up for this trial is actually a mix — one older V100 came in for a job and that could cause kernel fallback. We should pin the pool to a consistent SKU for the benchmark.
[01:49] Priya: Is that something we'd control from our side or Redwood?
[01:52] Elena: We can help pin it on the Redwood side for your dedicated pool; we just need to coordinate the capacity. For Private on-prem setups you'd control it. For this POC we can lock the SKU for the run.
[02:02] Samir: Also networking — Tom, once peering is live you'll see much fewer connection retries to the KV store, which will reduce overall latency. Right now the harness retries added ~60-80ms on some calls.
[02:12] Tom: Good to know, we'll prioritize getting peering scheduled. We'll open the firewall for the bastion and provide CIDR ranges by EOD.

[02:27] Lena: On results, I uploaded the small spreadsheet link to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/poc/nexahealth/results) — the summary: avg latency for 1k tokens was 220ms, p50 210ms, p95 360ms, p99 1.4s on the mixed-pool run.
[02:43] Samir: Those numbers are pretty reasonable for the mixed-run. With pinned A100s and KV cache we expect p99 to drop significantly. Elena, what's your config suggestion?
[02:51] Elena: Two immediate tunings: reduce batch size for latency-sensitive routes (we suggested batch_size=4 for conversational workloads), and enable KV prefix cache — that'll cut repeated token costs and lower tail. For throughput benchmarks you can bump batching up, but for your UI flows we recommend smaller batches. Also consider the 8-bit quantization profile we prepared — it's slightly higher memory but often faster on A100 kernels.
[03:18] Priya: Can you share that quant profile and the exact config in the repo?
[03:21] Elena: Yup — I'll drop the tuned config and the test harness link in the shared thread after the call (repo: https://git.redwood/inference/poc-harness).
[03:30] Tom: About security — Priya and I reviewed the checklist; we need SOC2 summary, network diagram, and details on key management. Do you have KMS/HSM integration docs?
[03:38] Samir: Yes, we'll send our security packet. It includes SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes (we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or HashiCorp HSM integrations), and the network diagram for the dedicated pool. I'll aim to get that out by Sunday (2026-12-27).
[03:52] Lena: Great. Also question on data residency — we need logs to stay in eu-west-1 for compliance, is that possible?
[03:58] Elena: For dedicated and private deployments we can pin region and storage to eu-west-1; for hosted there's a data residency option we can enable. We'll add the retention and audit log details in the packet.
[04:08] Priya: Re: benchmarks — when can we run the 10k token run? We want it to align with our maintenance downtime so it doesn't affect users.
[04:14] Samir: We can schedule it for 2026-12-30 during your maintenance window. Elena, can you own the run?
[04:19] Elena: Yep, I'll kick it off and post the raw results in the spreadsheet. I'll also try pinned A100s and the KV cache enabled so you get the low-tail numbers.
[04:27] Tom: One note — please throttle the run so it doesn't balloon costs unexpectedly; maybe cap concurrency to 6.
[04:33] Elena: Good call. We'll cap concurrency and annotate the cost estimate in the sheet.
[04:40] Samir: Any other blockers?
[04:42] Priya: We still need SSO/SAML integration for the console access before we sign off on the trial users. Is that a separate ticket?
[04:48] Samir: No problem — we support SAML 2.0. I'll include the metadata and the steps to configure it in the security packet. If you want, Solutions Eng can walk through the setup next week.
[04:59] Lena: Sounds good.
[05:01] Samir: Okay to recap: Samir will send security pack + network diagram by 12/27; Tom to provide CIDRs and bastion IPs by 12/29; Elena to run 10k token benchmark on 12/30 with pinned A100s, KV cache, limited concurrency and share results; Priya to confirm success criteria by 12/28. We'll reconvene after the benchmark or earlier if blockers pop up.
[05:20] Tom: Thanks all, we'll get the peering details today.
[05:24] Priya: Thanks, bye
[05:25] Elena: thanks, bye
[05:26] Samir: Thanks everyone, happy holidays
